dsh-plugin-macos
Native macOS superpowers for your DeepSeek Harness agent.

21 local tools for notifications, clipboard, screenshots, speech, keep-awake, dark mode,
Spotlight,
Shortcuts, AppleScript and Safari control.
English | 中文
**Your agent can write code. This gives it hands on your Mac.**

DeepSeek Harness (dsh) agents can already run bash, but every native macOS action still means
hand-w
riting AppleScript. ``dsh-plugin-macos`` packages the 21 chores you keep asking an agent to do into

typed, model-facing tools — notifications, clipboard, screenshots, speech, keep-awake, appearance,
S

potlight, Shortcuts, AppleScript and real Safari tabs. Everything runs locally through
``child_proce
ss`` and ``osascript``: no cloud service, no browser extension, no accessibility tree, no build step

,
no npm dependencies.
## Why this plugin
- **Broad but boring, on purpose.** It covers the long tail of daily Mac chores instead of one narro

w trick.
- **Safe by construction.** Every command uses argv arrays — never a shell string — so page

text, file names
and model output cannot inject shell syntax. Destructive verbs are not exposed.
-
**Zero-dependency, plain ESM.** ``git clone``, add the bundle, restart. No compile, no install scrip

ts.
- **Bilingual.** English and Chinese docs, plugin metadata and tool descriptions.
- **Honest abo

ut permissions.** Reads and writes are split into separate tools, and every macOS permission
prompt
is documented below.
## Tools (21)
### System
| Tool | What it does | Notes |
| ``macos_info`` | macOS version, chip, hostname, uptime, battery source, disk, memory | read-only |

| ``macos_network`` | hostname, primary interface, IPv4, current Wi-Fi SSID | read-only |
| ``macos

_processes`` | top processes by CPU or memory | read-only |
| ``macos_spotlight`` | search files wit

h Spotlight (``mdfind``) | read-only |
| ``macos_finder_path`` | POSIX path of the front Finder wind

ow | read-only |
| ``macos_frontmost_app`` | name of the frontmost application | read-only |
| ``mac
os_screenshot`` | capture the screen (or a region) to a PNG, return its path | Screen Recording |
### Everyday actions
| Tool | What it does | Notes |

| ``macos_notify`` | native notification banner with optional sound | Automation |
| ``macos_say`` |

speak text with the system voice | |
| ``macos_clipboard_read`` | read the clipboard text | read-on

ly |
| ``macos_clipboard_write`` | replace the clipboard text | |
| ``macos_volume`` | get or set ou

tput volume 0–100 | |
| ``macos_dark_mode`` | get or set dark mode | Automation: System Events |
| `

`macos_keep_awake`` | keep the Mac and display awake (``caffeinate``), stop, or report status | |
|

``macos_shortcuts`` | list the user's Shortcuts, or run one by name | |
| ``macos_open`` | open a UR

L, file, folder or application | |
| ``macos_applescript`` | run an AppleScript or JXA snippet and r
eturn stdout | powerful |
### Safari
| Tool | What it does | Notes |

| ``safari_tabs`` | list every Safari window and tab, plus the active tab | Automation: Safari |
| `

`safari_open`` | open a URL in a new tab or the current tab | |
| ``safari_page_text`` | read the vi

sible text of the front page | |
| ``safari_javascript`` | evaluate JavaScript in the front tab and
return the result | needs one Safari setting |
> Safari tools drive **your real, logged-in Safari** — no extension, no cloud browser, no API key.

gins** in the Web UI. Then ask your agent something like:

## Permissions
The first call to some tools triggers a one-time macOS consent prompt. Allow it for the application

that
hosts dsh (DeepSeek Harness, or your terminal if you launched dsh from one):
| Permission | Used by | Where to grant / revoke |

| Automation → Safari | ``safari_*`` tools | System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation |
| A

utomation → System Events | ``macos_dark_mode``, ``macos_frontmost_app`` | same |
| Automation → Fin

der | ``macos_finder_path`` | same |
| Screen Recording | ``macos_screenshot`` | System Settings → P

rivacy & Security → Screen Recording |
| Safari developer setting | ``safari_javascript`` | Safari →
Settings → Developer → **Allow JavaScript from Apple Events** |
Run `node scripts/doctor.mjs` from a checkout to exercise every permission-dependent tool once and s

ee
exactly which permissions macOS currently allows.
The plugin makes **no network requests** and stores **no telemetry**.
## Examples

- "Notify me when the build finishes, then say done out loud."
- "Read the Safari tab I am looking a

t and summarize it."
- "Start keep-awake, run the 40-minute test suite, then stop it."
